dr_desc_no_dr: No signs of diabetic retinopathy detected. The retina appears normal with no microaneurysms, haemorrhages, or exudates.
dr_desc_mild_dr: Mild non-proliferative DR. At least one microaneurysm present. Regular monitoring recommended.
dr_desc_moderate_dr: Moderate non-proliferative DR. Multiple microaneurysms, dot/blot haemorrhages, and possible hard exudates. Referral to ophthalmologist advised.
dr_desc_severe_dr: Severe non-proliferative DR (pre-proliferative). More than 20 intraretinal haemorrhages per quadrant, venous beading, or intraretinal microvascular abnormalities. Urgent referral required.
dr_desc_proliferative_dr: Proliferative DR. Neovascularisation present. Risk of vitreous haemorrhage and tractional retinal detachment. Immediate ophthalmology review and treatment required.
cdr_normal: CDR within normal limits (< 0.5). Low suspicion for glaucomatous optic neuropathy.
cdr_borderline: Borderline CDR (0.5 – 0.7). Careful monitoring and visual field testing recommended.
cdr_abnormal: Elevated CDR (> 0.7). Highly suspicious for glaucomatous damage. Formal glaucoma evaluation required.
gl_desc_no_glaucoma: No evidence of glaucomatous optic neuropathy.
gl_desc_suspect: Suspicious features for glaucoma. Full glaucoma workup including IOP, visual fields, and OCT RNFL recommended.
gl_desc_moderate: Moderate glaucomatous optic neuropathy with rim thinning. IOP management and regular follow-up essential.
gl_desc_advanced: Advanced glaucomatous damage. Significant rim loss. Urgent IOP reduction and specialist management required.
follow_up_1: Follow-up in 6–12 months. Optimise glycaemic and blood pressure control.
follow_up_4: Immediate ophthalmology referral. Possible laser or surgical intervention.
rec_glaucoma_eval: Optic disc: Formal glaucoma evaluation (IOP, visual fields, OCT-RNFL) recommended.
rec_lesion_urgent: Lesion burden elevated — urgent ophthalmology review advised.
